title: How many bytes is café?
hook: Text is stored as numbers. Does every character get the same amount of room?

knows: a byte holds one small number
doesNotKnow: that UTF-8 uses 1 to 4 bytes per character, so length in bytes is not length in characters

misconception: One character is always one byte.
objective: The learner can say that café is 4 characters but 5 bytes in UTF-8, because é takes two bytes while c, a and f take one, and that other characters take three or four.

claims.text: Stored as UTF-8, café (4 characters) takes 5 bytes.
claims.source: Node: Buffer.byteLength('café') = 5, [...'café'].length = 4 (é as the single code point U+00E9, NFC). Demo.tsx computes with TextEncoder. Builder re-ran in Node 2026-10-13.

claims.text: In UTF-8, é is two bytes, C3 A9.
claims.source: Node: Buffer.from('é') = <c3 a9>. RFC 3629 section 3: U+0080 to U+07FF encode as 2 bytes (110xxxxx 10xxxxxx); U+00E9 -> C3 A9.

claims.text: c, a and f take one byte each in UTF-8, the same codes as ASCII (63, 61, 66 in hex).
claims.source: RFC 3629 section 1/3: U+0000 to U+007F are encoded as one byte identical to US-ASCII. Node: Buffer.from('caf') = <63 61 66>.

claims.text: 世 takes three bytes in UTF-8 (E4 B8 96) and 😀 takes four (F0 9F 98 80).
claims.source: Node: Buffer.from('世') = <e4 b8 96> (U+4E16), Buffer.from('😀') = <f0 9f 98 80> (U+1F600). RFC 3629 section 3 table.

claims.text: UTF-8 gives every ASCII character (English letters, digits, spaces and basic punctuation) one byte, and accented letters, emoji and most other characters two, three or four, so counting bytes and counting characters give different answers.
claims.source: RFC 3629 (Yergeau 2003), section 3: each code point is encoded in 1 to 4 octets. 'Characters' here means Unicode code points; the stage shows only precomposed characters. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 9): Pass 9 re-check: stage reveal still says 'UTF-8 gives the plain English letters one byte and other characters two, three or four' (Demo.tsx line 52). Still false for digits, spaces and punctuation (1 byte, RFC 3629 s.3). Dispute stands; same fix as pass 8. | BUILDER 2026-10-13: stage and claim reworded per fact-check; needs re-verification.

claims.text: UTF-8 is a common way to save text.
claims.source: WHATWG Encoding Standard requires UTF-8 for new content; W3Techs usage survey reports UTF-8 on about 98% of websites (2024). Learner-visible wording kept to 'a common way'.

recall.question: Stored as UTF-8, the word naïve has 5 characters. How many bytes does it take?
recall.why: n, a, v, e take one byte each; ï, like é, takes two (C3 AF). 4 + 2 = 6 bytes for 5 characters.
